Limited police investigative techniques, reliance on circumstantial and scientific evidence

surface_summary: Daniel Purcell disappears during a yacht voyage from Sennen Cove to Penzance. His companion, Mr. Varney, claims Purcell landed at Penzance and later at other ports, supported by letters purportedly from Purcell. Suspicious circumstances and scientific evidence suggest Purcell's death and Varney's deception.
accepted_facts: Purcell and Varney sailed alone on the yacht from Sennen Cove
Purcell was last seen by Varney during the voyage
Letters purportedly from Purcell were received after his disappearance
Scientific examination found a blood stain on the yacht's sail and a cork button with marine worm tube from Purcell's coat
inferred_conclusions: Purcell landed at Penzance and other ports after the voyage
Purcell is alive and hiding in the Eastern Counties
Varney is a loyal friend trying to protect Purcell
mechanism_description: Varney murdered Purcell during the yacht voyage by shooting him and disposing of his body weighted with an iron half-hundred weight. He fabricated evidence of Purcell's survival by forging letters and inventing false sightings at ports. Scientific evidence, including the blood stain on the sail and the cork button with a marine worm tube found on the sea bottom near Wolf Rock, proved Purcell's death and Varney's guilt.
delivery_path: Varney shoots Purcell on the yacht during fog near Wolf Rock
Varney attaches Purcell's body to an iron weight and throws it overboard
Varney cleans blood stains from the sail and fabricates a story of Purcell landing at Penzance
Varney forges letters in Purcell's handwriting and posts them from distant locations
Scientific evidence including the cork button with marine worm tube is found on the sea bottom near Wolf Rock
Investigation reveals missing ballast weight and rope from the yacht
Varney's forged letters and false sightings are exposed, confirming Purcell's death
outcome_result: Purcell is conclusively proven dead and Varney is identified as his murderer, though legal proof of murder is complicated by lack of direct evidence.

false_assumption.statement: Purcell landed at Penzance and other ports after the yacht voyage and is alive.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Varney, the sole companion, testified to Purcell's landing and subsequent sightings; letters purportedly from Purcell were received after his disappearance. These facts appeared to confirm Purcell's survival.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: Varney fabricated the sightings and forged the letters to conceal Purcell's murder and death during the voyage.

supporting_points: Margaret's suspicions about her husband's disappearance
Her emotional distress and desire for freedom
Her possible motive related to Purcell's secretive and brutal nature
Her access to the letters and knowledge of the case
false_solution.the_one_flaw: There is no evidence that Margaret had opportunity or motive to commit the murder; all incriminating evidence points to Varney.

red_herrings.description: Reports and Varney's testimony that Purcell was seen at Falmouth and Ipswich after the disappearance.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: Varney, as the fabricator of these false sightings
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: These sightings were invented by Varney to mislead the investigation and divert suspicion from the murder.

red_herrings.description: The mysterious letter and enclosures received by Mr. Penfield from Purcell.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: Purcell, suggesting illicit activities or secret communications
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The letter contained forged bank-note blanks and was part of Varney's scheme to expose Purcell and cover up the murder.

closed_circle.rationale: Only Varney was present on the yacht with Purcell, had opportunity and motive, and all fabricated evidence and scientific findings point to him as the murderer.

time_windows: Voyage duration from Sennen to Penzance
Investigation period from disappearance to recovery of evidence

inference_path.observation: Varney claims Purcell landed at Penzance and other ports
inference_path.correction: Scientific and testimonial evidence disproves these sightings
inference_path.effect: Purcell likely never landed and is dead
required_evidence: Captain's report of the steamer Hedwig passenger list showing no Purcell
Witness statements denying Purcell's presence at Falmouth and Ipswich

inference_path.observation: Letters purportedly from Purcell received after disappearance
inference_path.correction: Microscopic and forensic examination shows letters are forged
inference_path.effect: Letters are fabrications to conceal Purcell's death
required_evidence: Microscopic analysis of postmarks on letters showing lithographic forgery
Comparison of handwriting and ink with known samples

inference_path.observation: Blood stain and hand print found on yacht's sail
inference_path.correction: Hand print matches Varney's maimed finger
inference_path.effect: Varney was present at the time of Purcell's death and involved
required_evidence: Chemical test of blood stain on sail
Visual and microscopic comparison of hand print with Varney's finger

inference_path.observation: Missing ballast weight and cut rope from yacht
inference_path.correction: Weight and rope likely used to sink Purcell's body
inference_path.effect: Body disposed of weighted to sink at sea bottom
required_evidence: Inventory check of yacht gear showing missing weight and rope
Witness testimony of yacht condition before and after voyage

inference_path.observation: Cork button with marine worm tube found on sea bottom
inference_path.correction: Button is from Purcell's oilskin coat and has been underwater for months
inference_path.effect: Purcell's coat and body have been at sea bottom near Wolf Rock
required_evidence: Identification of button embroidery as Purcell's
Expert analysis of marine worm tube composition and origin

inference_path.observation: Varney's sudden disappearance from social circles
inference_path.correction: Varney's disappearance coincides with investigation progress
inference_path.effect: Varney attempts to avoid detection and consequences
required_evidence: Witness statements of Varney's last known whereabouts

inference_path.observation: Varney appears on lugger near Wolf Rock during search
inference_path.correction: Varney's presence confirms proximity to crime scene and body disposal
inference_path.effect: Varney is implicated as murderer and responsible for body disposal
required_evidence: Eyewitness account of Varney boarding search boat
Matching of hand print and blood evidence to Varney

discriminating_test.design: A search expedition using creepers and trawl-rope is conducted near Wolf Rock to recover physical evidence. The search focuses on the area identified by the marine worm tube analysis and the missing ballast weight. The test observes if the body or identifiable remains can be recovered to conclusively prove death.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test reveals the location of Purcell's body and physical evidence linking Varney to the murder and disposal.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Recovery of Purcell's identifiable remains, such as the oilskin coat with the button and skull with bullet hole, from the sea bottom near Wolf Rock.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given all necessary clues including Varney's suspicious behavior, the forged letters, the blood stain on the sail, the missing ballast weight and rope, and the scientific evidence of the marine worm tube on Purcell's button. The false sightings and letters are exposed as fabrications. The reader could deduce that Purcell was murdered during the yacht voyage and that Varney concealed the crime by fabricating evidence of Purcell's survival.
